channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: The euro fell 0.8% to USD 1.1161 in Asian trading on 5 October, its lowest level since May 2025, on investor concern about political uncertainty and tight public finances in several euro-area countries, Handelsblatt reports.
item.description:
The spread on French government bonds over German bonds reached its highest level since 2011 on Friday, Handelsblatt reports; MarketScreener puts the 10-year spread above 150 basis points, as markets worry about the French government's ability to pass its budget and prevent the deficit from reaching 6.5% without one. The euro recovered some losses during the day and then fell again after Spain's Prime Minister announced new elections, and has declined about 3% since the end of August, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reports. The Guardian reports a drop of about eight cents from a peak of USD 1.20 in January. A stronger dollar also weighs on the currency, Handelsblatt reports. The reporting does not give the euro's closing level or moves against other currencies.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The move is an intraday low on one day; the trend since August and since January is measured from different starting points by different outlets. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a weaker euro makes dollar-priced imports such as oil and many chemical raw materials more expensive in euro terms, while making euro-area exports cheaper. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, the effect on input costs arrives through dollar-denominated feedstocks, and on sales through exports from euro-area plants. Points that may be worth considering include whether the French budget is passed, and how much of current raw-material contracts is priced in dollars.

Handelsblatt | MarketScreener | Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung | The Guardian

item.title: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called a snap general election for 29 November, three days after government legislation on housing costs was defeated in parliament, The Financial Times reports.
item.description:
The FT calls the vote a gamble that could, if it backfires, open the way for a coalition of conservatives and right-wing populists to take power in the EU's fourth-largest economy. The early election threatens to pause part of the regulatory agenda at a time of high energy prices caused by the war in Iran, El Correo reports: the ecological transition ministry still has open regulations on connecting new projects to the grid and on investments in renewables, storage and data centres, including a royal decree on data centres' access to the grid; the problem for companies is less cancellation than delay. The acting government wants to approve the two housing decrees again with changes, which would leave the rental market under the decrees' terms for at least two or three months, ABC reports. The reporting does not give a list of the pending energy regulations or polling.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The date is fixed; the outcome and the fate of the pending rules are not. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a pause in grid-connection and investment rules delays decisions on projects with long horizons, and a change of government can alter energy and housing policy together. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, Spain's construction and industrial demand depends partly on how quickly grid connections and housing measures are settled. Points that may be worth considering include which energy decrees are approved before the vote, and whether housing measures survive the election.

The Financial Times | El Correo | ABC.es

item.title: Merz and Macron have written to Commission President von der Leyen proposing new EU trade instruments, including one to be activated quickly if vital supplies are restricted, with measures up to an immediate cut-off from the internal market.
item.description:
The letter proposes two instruments, one for diversification so that companies do not become too dependent on suppliers from individual countries, and an expedited procedure to exclude another country from the single market, Handelsblatt reports. It states that the instrument is "country agnostic", but analysts see it as a response to Beijing's restrictions on exports of rare earths and magnets last year, The Financial Times reports. Commercial Times describes the proposal as still in the policy recommendation stage and reports that the two leaders advocate activation through a "reverse qualified majority"; Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reports that the Commission should be able to activate it independently, with member states able to prevent this only by qualified majority. Countermeasures could extend to excluding individual companies, Handelsblatt reports. The Commission said the letter aligned with von der Leyen's stance on competitiveness and her approach to trading partners, including China, Nikkei Asian Review reports. Separately, during a state visit to Spain, Macron called on the EU to protect its markets against Chinese competition, and Yahoo! Taiwan puts the EU's trade deficit with China at around EUR 1 billion a day. The reporting does not give a timetable or a legal basis.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

This is a proposal from two governments, not a measure; no instrument, trigger or product scope exists yet. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a faster and broader EU response tool raises the stakes of trade disputes with China in both directions, including the risk of countermeasures on European exports and on raw materials that China controls. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, the diversification instrument is the part closest to supply chains, because it would address dependence on single-country suppliers of inputs. Points that may be worth considering include how the Commission and other member states respond, and whether the proposal features at the EU–China talks in Beijing.

Handelsblatt | The Financial Times | Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung | Handelsblatt | Commercial Times | Nikkei Asian Review | Yahoo! Taiwan

item.title: Yemeni government troops supported by the Saudi Arabian military alliance announced they had brought the Bab al-Mandab strait under their control, and Chancellor Merz said he is cautiously optimistic that the Red Sea situation could ease.
item.description:
Merz also said that the Strait of Hormuz must be permanently reopened, even without tariffs being levied there, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reports. Middle East crude export figures from Kpler include flows via the Red Sea, a route increasingly used to bypass the blockade Iran is attempting to impose on Hormuz, Hürriyet Daily News reports. The reporting does not say who controlled the strait before, whether the announcement has been confirmed by other parties, or whether shipping traffic, freight rates or insurance premiums on the route have changed. The control claim rests on one report.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The control claim is the troops' own announcement, and the only reaction reported is a statement of cautious optimism; the sources report no effect on shipping. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, Bab al-Mandab is the southern entrance to the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe, so security there affects both the Red Sea bypass for Gulf crude and container traffic. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, a safer Red Sea route would bear on freight times and costs for raw materials and finished goods moving between Asia and Europe. Points that may be worth considering include whether shipping lines and insurers change their routing or war-risk terms, and whether the announcement is confirmed.

Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung | Hürriyet Daily News

item.title: India's Cabinet-approved Bhavya Rasayan scheme aims to set up three major chemical parks, with INR 10bn of central funding and at least INR 5bn from each participating state, and a minister urges states and industry to take part.
item.description:
Anupriya Patel, Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, urged state governments and domestic industry to take part in the scheme, which the Cabinet approved to drive the growth of the petrochemical and chemical sector, The Hindu BusinessLine reports. The reporting does not give the locations of the parks, the selection process for states, a timetable, the expected investment by companies, or the product groups the parks will host. It rests on one source.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The amounts are public funding commitments, not capacity, and the reporting does not say whether participating states or sites have been chosen. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, dedicated chemical parks with shared infrastructure are a common instrument for attracting both domestic and foreign producers, and they tend to cluster upstream and downstream production. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, India is a growing market and a growing source of chemical intermediates, so new parks can affect both local raw-material availability and competition from Indian producers. Points that may be worth considering include which states join and which product chains the parks target.

The Hindu BusinessLine

item.title: BloombergNEF projects global oil refining capacity to rise by 4.2 million barrels a day in 2026–2030, mostly in Africa and Asia-Pacific, while retirements mainly in Europe and North America remove about 200,000 barrels a day.
item.description:
According to BNEF's Global Oil Refining Outlook, around 2.9 million barrels a day is expected to come from expansions at existing refineries in Africa, India, China, other parts of Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Latin America, and newly built refineries are expected to add around 1.5 million barrels a day, mainly in Africa, India, China and other parts of Asia-Pacific, Anadolu Agency reports. Dünya reports that around 95% of net growth will come from Africa and Asia-Pacific, that the net increase would be 162% more than in the previous five-year period, and that India and China will step up short-term investments. The reporting does not give a split between fuels and petrochemical output, or the effect of the current war on the projection.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

These are projections of capacity, not output, and the regional split is BNEF's. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, refining capacity growing in Asia and Africa while Europe retires capacity moves the supply of refined products and refinery-linked petrochemical feedstocks further from European users. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, solvents, resins and other hydrocarbon-derived raw materials made close to refineries would increasingly come from Asian and Middle Eastern sources, which adds freight and route exposure. Points that may be worth considering include which European refineries are named for closure, and how integrated refining and chemical projects in Asia shape import competition.

Anadolu Agency | Dünya Gazetesi

item.title: Car registrations in China fell 24% year on year in August to 1.5 million, AlixPartners suggested before the summer that 2026 sales could fall 10%, and fewer domestic sales push makers to seek exports, Il Sole 24 Ore reports.
item.description:
AlixPartners' Dario Duse describes the market as in sharp contraction, down 18% in the first four months with a partial correction in recent months but still in negative territory, and names the end of incentives, the economy and the property market as causes; Il Sole 24 Ore says the market has entered a phase of declining sales, price wars and consolidation, and that exports are estimated to grow to up to 10 million vehicles in 2026. In Europe, Chinese brands accounted for 11% of new car sales in August, according to the market research firm Dataforce, La Vanguardia reports. In Russia, Chinese brands account for more than 40% of the new-car market excluding vehicles sold under local names, according to an industry analyst quoted by The Moscow Times. The reporting does not give Chinese production figures or export figures to date.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The August fall is a measured registration figure; the full-year and export numbers are projections, and the European and Russian shares come from different sources and measures. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a contracting home market with spare capacity tends to push price competition into export markets, and the trade defence measures being discussed in Europe are partly a response to that. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, Chinese vehicle exports shift assembly volume, and the bonding and sealing applications that go with it, from European plants to Chinese ones. Points that may be worth considering include whether Chinese exports grow as projected, and how European trade measures change the mix of imported vehicles.

Il Sole 24 Ore | La Vanguardia | The Moscow Times

item.title: Transaction volume on the German real-estate investment market totalled EUR 23.1bn to the end of September 2026, about 3% below the previous year's result, according to an analysis by BNP Paribas Real Estate.
item.description:
Residential remains the strongest asset class at EUR 5.9bn but for the moment registers a fall of a good 5% year on year, while commercial real estate reached EUR 17.1bn, down 2%, Wallstreet:online reports. BNP Paribas Real Estate describes the environment as continuously challenging, and says closing momentum, at around 1,050 transactions, is the strongest since 2022. The reporting does not give third-quarter figures on their own, a breakdown of the commercial segment by office, logistics or retail, or construction starts. It rests on one source.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

These are investment transactions, which measure capital flows rather than construction activity, and the number of deals is the highest since 2022 while the value is lower than a year earlier. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, investment volume leads new development and refurbishment decisions by months, so a market that is active in deal count but lower in value suggests buyers are trading smaller or repriced assets. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, German construction demand for sealants, flooring and tile adhesives depends on building and renovation activity that follows these investment decisions. Points that may be worth considering include whether building permits and construction orders confirm a turn, and how the residential decline relates to new-build versus existing stock.

Wallstreet:online

item.title: German new-car registrations rose 12.8% year on year in September to 235,500, according to the Federal Motor Transport Authority, while passenger-car production was unchanged at 392,200 and total orders fell just over 13%, VDA reports.
item.description:
The share of battery-electric cars in the total car market rose to 34.5% in September from 19.3% a year earlier, while the plug-in hybrid share fell to 10.8% from 11.8%, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reports. On the production side, the German automotive association VDA reports 3.03 million passenger cars built in the first nine months, 4% fewer than a year earlier and 15% below 2019. Exports rose 1% in September to 288,800 but are down 4% over nine months at 2.29 million. Domestic orders rose 4% in September while orders from abroad fell 16%; German manufacturers' domestic orders for battery-electric cars rose 79%. The reporting does not give the share of September registrations built in Germany, or the reason for the fall in foreign orders.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Registrations measure demand in Germany and production measures output from German plants, so they are different quantities, and the sources do not explain why registrations rose while production was unchanged. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a domestic market growing on battery-electric cars can be supplied partly by imports, so registrations alone overstate the work reaching German assembly lines, and weak foreign orders point to softer output ahead. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, bonding and sealing demand at German plants follows production and orders more than registrations, while the drivetrain shift changes which battery and lightweighting applications are used. Points that may be worth considering include whether foreign orders recover in the fourth quarter, and how much of the battery-electric growth is built in Germany.

Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung | VDA

item.title: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil is launching a tax, paid by companies, on packaging, films and composite packaging with over 5% plastic content, expected to raise EUR 805 million next year and a good EUR 1.4 billion a year from 2028.
item.description:
The tax causes considerable effort for both the federal government and businesses, Handelsblatt reports: the Finance Ministry expects expenditures of EUR 284 million in the federal budget up to 2029, incurred among others by the Information Technology Center and customs. The reporting does not give the tax rate or how it is calculated, whether recycled plastic content is treated differently, the start date, the legislative stage, or which packaging types are exempt. It rests on one source.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The revenue figures are expectations, not a measured volume, and the design details reported are the scope (packaging, films and composite packaging), the threshold of more than 5% plastic content, and that companies pay. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, a tax levied on plastic content acts as a material-selection instrument whatever its fiscal purpose, because it changes the relative cost of plastic, paper and mixed-material formats. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, composite packaging is held together by laminating adhesives and coatings, so a threshold on plastic content reaches back into how laminates are built and whether the bonding layer counts towards the plastic share. Points that may be worth considering include how the tax base is defined in the legislative text, and whether brand owners respond by redesigning formats to fall below the threshold.

Handelsblatt

item.title: Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser says the war has reduced oil supply from the Middle East by almost 3bn barrels and that rebuilding inventories depleted during the conflict could take up to two years, The Financial Times reports.
item.description:
Nasser said the lost volume is equivalent to around 50% of the refined fuels and crude oil that would have passed through the Strait of Hormuz during the seven-month war between Iran, Israel and the US. Over 1bn barrels have been drawn from reserves, with governments releasing more than 300mn barrels from strategic reserves, the FT reports, and Nasser estimated that less than 6bn barrels of commercial inventories remain, the vast majority not practically available. Current export flows are a separate measure: the seven-day moving average of crude exports from the region was 18.3 million barrels a day on 30 September on provisional Kpler data, BNN Bloomberg reports. In the IEA's March emergency release of 400 million barrels, European countries contributed 107.5 million, of which 32.7 million came from state-owned emergency stocks and the rest from mandatory industry stocks, according to Euronews, so the IEA total is not the same measure as the FT's figure for government releases. The reporting does not give how Nasser's figures were calculated, the split between crude and refined products, or the inventory level before the war.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The 3bn-barrel and two-year figures are a producer's estimates, not measured data; the Kpler figures measure current export flows and are a different quantity, so recovering flows and depleted stocks are not combined here. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, low inventories leave the market with less buffer against new disruptions even as flows recover, which tends to keep prices sensitive to each incident. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, the buffer question matters for petrochemical raw materials and solvents, whose prices follow crude and refined products. Points that may be worth considering include whether other producers or the IEA publish comparable inventory estimates, and how quickly commercial stocks are rebuilt once flows hold.

The Financial Times | BNN Bloomberg | Euronews

item.title: Cefic's Chemicals Trends summary report finds that EU27 chemical production declined by 2.0% between January and July 2026 compared with 2025, with weak demand, and says a broad-based and sustainable recovery has yet to emerge.
item.description:
The European Chemical Industry Council says the EU27 chemical industry remains under pressure despite improving confidence, and that structural competitiveness pressures continued to intensify. The report is based on Eurostat data and covers the economic and business climate, energy prices, output, total sales, extra-EU trade, consumption and capacity utilisation across the 27 member states. The reporting does not give the figures for sales, trade, energy prices or capacity utilisation, a breakdown by chemical segment or country, or whether the decline was larger in the most recent months. It rests on one source, the association's own summary.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The production figure is a measured volume over seven months, and Cefic itself pairs it with improving confidence, so sentiment and output point in different directions. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, a fall in European chemical output alongside weak demand can mean lower utilisation at producers of the intermediates and polymers that formulators buy, which tends to keep pressure on producers to rationalise capacity. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, a shrinking European production base raises the question of how much raw-material supply shifts to imports and over what distance. Points that may be worth considering include whether the full Eurostat series shows a turn in the latest months, and which upstream product groups are contracting most.

Cefic
